paper_title: How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media
caption: The average similarities between the headlines from different seasons
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how average headline similarity varies across different seasonal time-gap bins. The x-axis is labeled “Δ Days” and uses a categorical, evenly spaced set of five interval bins shown as tick labels: “(0,90]”, “(90,180]”, “(180,270]”, “(270,360]”, and “(360,450]”. The y-axis is labeled “Avg. similarity (10e-2)”, uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about 1.67 to 1.85, with visible numeric tick labels at approximately 1.70, 1.75, 1.80, and 1.85. A single light-blue dash-dot line with circular markers is plotted, accompanied by a light-blue shaded band around the line indicating a narrow vertical range around the mean at each x-bin. The marked average similarity starts near 1.84 at (0,90], decreases to about 1.80 at (90,180], drops further to roughly 1.73 at (180,270], rises slightly to about 1.74 at (270,360], and then declines to around 1.68 at (360,450].
